Want to help teams spend time wisely? We’re hiring.
text: Want to help teams spend time wisely? We’re hiring. We believe work should be fun, meaningful, and challenging. Our mission is to help teams succeed by encouraging the respectful and intentional use of time, and that mission speaks to everything we do as a company. View job openings How we work Harvest is a small but mighty global workforce. We value self-discipline, scrappiness and a genuine curiosity to learn from one another. Motivated by excellence and collaboration, our people are the engine that fuels our success. A global team We hire amazing talent, no matter where they happen to call home. Our team is spread across 9 countries and 11 different timezones, resulting in a rich working environment where diverse perspectives, backgrounds, and opinions inform every discussion and decision. Flexible working Harvest started as a remote team, and over the last 17 years we’ve mastered the art of remote working. We’ve embraced its advantages, found creative ways to overcome its challenges, and take pride in being an efficient and thriving remote-first team. Investing in people We care about providing our team with opportunities for learning and career growth. Every Harvester receives an annual learning stipend, and we support their attendance to a conference related to their role per year. Both internally and externally, we are committed to supporting our Harvesters in developing their skills and their careers. Giving Back We believe in the importance of giving back to our communities. Our Harvest for Good program aims to make a positive impact through a combination of charitable giving and community involvement. Every month, we make a meaningful donation to a different cause Harvesters feel passionate about, and we also match personal donations and volunteer hours. In 2023, our contributions totalled over $750,000. Striving for excellence We build best-in-class products loved by thousands of businesses across the world. We put a great deal of effort and intentionality into the work we do, and care deeply about our craft. Grounded in sustainable growth We don’t grow or hire for growth’s sake. Harvest is a profitable, stable business that scales intentionally. Our principles Bring kindness We uplift and treat each other with dignity. We show up with thoughtfulness and humility, listen and learn, empathize, and strive to be of service. We recognize that people matter, and are deliberate with how we engage in the world. Cultivate collaboration We foster an environment of creativity, respect, and trust. To do this, we stay curious, build connections, honor expertise, work through challenges together, and strive to understand different perspectives and ideas. Honor time We're thoughtful about how we work. We work with intention and design for flexibility while prioritizing shared goals. To bring wisdom to how we spend time, we're collaborative, considerate, and impactful with our shared time. Innovate with a learning mindset We create new things, discover new ideas, and explore new ways of doing. We recognize that learning is a lifelong endeavor. This is why we value experimentation, curiosity, and taking risks to create and grow. Seek impact We do things that matter, knowing that they make a difference. To do this, we set worthwhile goals and create plans of action. Our actions matter, not just intentions. Because of this, we strive to do good in our work and in the world. Perks & benefits Harvest offers competitive compensation and generous benefits so you have all you need to grow and succeed. Competitive and Fair Compensation We pay at the top of the New York City market for all roles independent of your location, and use third-party data to ensure salaries stay competitive. Health & Dental * We provide 100% coverage of health insurance premiums across our medical, dental, and vision base plan offerings for you, your spouse, and your dependents. Time Off We offer 15 days of vacation during your first year, and an additional two days per year of tenure until you reach 20 days, plus national holidays in your location. We also provide flexible personal and sick days, and a week off for Winter Break between Christmas and New Years. Family Support We support new parents with 16 weeks of paid maternity or paternity leave. In addition, Harvesters get access to Maven, a family health platform offering support services for preconcepcion, maternity, parenting, and pediatric care. Professional Development We believe in the importance of professional development, so we provide all Harvesters with a yearly education stipend of $1000 and support attendance to a conference relevant to your role each year. Work Setup We’ll provide you with the right tools for your role, including a company-issued computer and a standing desk and ergonomic chair. And if you prefer to not work from home, we offer you a monthly $400 stipend towards a co-working space. Bonus Structure We reward and recognize Harvesters for their contribution to our success with individual performance bonuses based on achieved work outcomes, and a company bonus program based on our business performance. Caring for You We provide Harvesters with access to Compsych, an Employee Assistance Program offering a variety of services to support your wellbeing. Some resources include emotional support, financial advice, legal guidance, and work and lifestyle support. Vacation Fund We want to make sure that you take time away from work. After 4 years at Harvest, you’ll receive $5,000 per year to spend on a trip (increased to $8,000 if you’re bringing kids). Referral Program We’ll award you a bonus of $1,750 and a $250 charitable donation if a candidate you refer for a new role joins the team. Retirement * We invest in your future through 401k planning, with a 6% company match after 3 months with the company. * Some of the benefits described are only available to Harvesters based in the U.S. Benefits information for Harvesters outside the U.S. will be provided to individuals who interview for those roles. Can Hanzo handle Slack, Teams, and Google Workspace data? Yes. Hanzo is built specifically for collaboration data from these platforms. Denunciar este empleo En HF Solutions desarrollamos y evolucionamos soluciones de software sobre la nube y para productos mobile, con foco en sistemas transaccionales y plataformas que escalan. Buscamos un/a Desarrollador/a Fullstack Semi Senior para integrarse a un equipo que participa en todo el ciclo de vida del desarrollo: desde el levantamiento de necesidades y el diseño técnico hasta el despliegue y la operación. El objetivo del rol es construir aplicaciones web end-to-end (frontend y backend), conectando distintas fuentes de datos y servicios de terceros vía APIs REST, y asegurando calidad con buenas prácticas, pruebas, documentación y revisión de código. RESPONSABILIDADES PRINCIPALESEn el rol de desarrollador/a Fullstack, nosotros nos enfocamos en que el equipo entregue funcionalidades completas, consistentes y mantenibles, participando en todo el ciclo de vida del software.Desarrollar funcionalidades frontend y backend de acuerdo con los requerimientos del proyecto.Construir e integrar APIs REST conectando distintas fuentes de datos y servicios de terceros.Participar en la definición de la arquitectura técnica junto con el ArquitectoEscribir código mantenible, testeado y documentado, alineado a las buenas prácticas definidas por el equipo.Colaborar con Diseño UI/UX para implementar interfaces fieles al diseño entregado.Participar en code reviews y en la mejora continua de procesos de desarrollo.Dar soporte y resolver incidencias en ambientes de producción cuando corresponda.Además, nosotros buscamos que el/la profesional contribuya activamente a la calidad, la trazabilidad de cambios y la estabilidad del producto, desde el desarrollo hasta la operación. REQUISITOS TÉCNICOSExperiencia como desarrollador/a Fullstack de al menos 3 años (perfil semi senior).Manejo de al menos un framework frontend moderno: React y Angular.Backend con Java (Spring Boot).Conocimiento de nube, idealmente AWS.Experiencia con bases de datos relacionales y no relacionales: SQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, entre otras.Conocimiento de control de versiones: Git y flujos colaborativos como Git Flow, pull requests y revisiones.Nociones de despliegue y ambientes cloud: AWS, Azure o GCP.Habilidades blandasAutonomía para resolver problemas técnicos con criterio propio.Capacidad para comunicar avances y bloqueos de forma clara al equipo y a la jefatura de proyecto.Adaptabilidad para trabajar en distintos stacks tecnológicos según el cliente o producto.Nos importa que nosotros podamos confiar en tu criterio técnico, tu responsabilidad en la entrega y tu colaboración diaria para asegurar que las soluciones funcionen en ambientes reales y se mantengan a lo largo del tiempo. REQUISITOS DESEABLESConocimiento de Docker / contenedores y prácticas de CI/CD.Experiencia previa colaborando directamente con equipos de UI/UX para traducir diseños a implementaciones.Valoramos especialmente a quienes ya han trabajado con automatización de despliegues y procesos de integración continua, ya que acelera la entrega y mejora la estabilidad. Every day is an opportunity to learn something new and make a real impact." Our Core Values Six commitments every Hatcher lives by, every single day. Radical Transparency Say the hard thing. Share the full picture. When everyone operates from the same truth, better decisions happen naturally. Create Raving Fans Good enough is not the goal. We do work that clients remember, talk about, and come back for. Iterate to Improve Ship it, learn from it, make it better. We value momentum over perfection and curiosity over comfort. Think Like Entrepreneurs Treat every project like it is yours. Ask the uncomfortable questions, take the calculated risk, and care about the outcome. Our Best Asset Is Our People The work is only as good as the people behind it. We invest in each other and build careers worth having. We Own the Outcome When something goes sideways, we do not point fingers. We figure out what happened and fix it together. Creating Tomorrow's Tech Leaders Today As a Hatcher, you are part of something bigger. HatchFutures opens real doors for the next generation of tech talent through mentorship, education, and opportunity. The work you do here matters beyond the job. Visit HatchFutures Life at HatchWorks A glimpse into what it looks and feels like to be a Hatcher. View photo View photo View photo View photo View photo Now Hiring Open Positions Become a Hatcher. We are always looking for curious, driven people who want to do real work and grow with a team that actually cares. See Open Positions Read our blog What Do You Do With the Hours AI Gives Back? Andy Smith The New Attack Surface Is Everything Your Agent Can Chain Its Way To: Cogent’s Anirudh Ravula on AI Security Andy Smith AI Coding Agent Costs: The Hidden Harness Tax Andy Smith Your AI Pilot Worked. So Why Isn’t It in Production? Andy Smith Frequently Asked Questions Everything you want to know about working at HatchWorks AI. All Applying Hiring Process Culture Growth Remote Work How do I apply for a job at HatchWorks? Head to our open positions page and submit your application directly. Include your resume and anything else that shows what you bring to the table. No need for a lengthy cover letter — just make sure what you send actually reflects you. Can I apply for more than one role at a time? Yes. Apply to as many roles as you genuinely fit. Just make sure each application speaks to that specific position — a generic submission that ignores the job description tends to get skipped. What if I do not meet all the qualifications listed? You can still apply. Meeting the minimum requirements is important, but we also look at how people think, what they have built, and how they approach problems. If you are close and genuinely interested, send it in. What types of roles are available at HatchWorks? We hire across engineering, product design, UX, AI, project management, sales, and operations. The mix changes constantly as we grow. The best way to see what is open right now is to check our jobs board. Are international candidates considered? Yes. HatchWorks works with talent across Latin America and beyond. Whether it is possible for a specific role depends on the position and work authorization. The job posting will usually clarify location requirements. What does the hiring process look like? It varies by role but generally follows this path: Recruiter screen Online skills assessment Technical interview Interview with a HatchWorks hiring manager Client interview We keep you informed at every stage and give you an estimated timeline so nothing feels like a black box. How long does the hiring process take? It depends on the role and how quickly each stage moves. We do our best to keep things moving and will always communicate an expected timeline. If things take longer than expected, we will tell you why. How will I know if I am selected for an interview? We will reach out by phone or email to schedule next steps. Make sure the contact info on your application is current and that your inbox is not filtering us out. How much English do I need? Clear communication is core to how we work. Most client-facing roles require strong spoken and written English. Internal roles may require less, but a functional level is generally expected. The job posting will specify if there are particular language requirements. How would you describe the culture at HatchWorks? Honest, fast-moving, and human. We are an AI-first company that still puts people at the center. The team is small enough that your work is visible and your voice matters, but established enough that you have real structure and support around you. We have won four Best Places to Work awards, and the reason is pretty simple: we actually invest in the people here. What is a Hatcher? A Hatcher is how we refer to the people who work here. It is not just a label. It describes someone who is passionate, selfless, curious, creative, and driven. Someone who builds things people love and cares about more than just their own output. Does HatchWorks do community work? Yes, and it is not performative. HatchWorks is committed to creating opportunities for young and emerging talent in technology, particularly in communities where access is limited. That mission shapes how we think about hiring, education, and what it means to be a tech company with actual roots somewhere. Where can I learn more about HatchWorks values and culture? The Our Culture page on the HatchWorks site is the best place to start. You can also ask directly during your interviews. We do not hide who we are. What does professional development look like here? We invest in annual training for every Hatcher. We also run a Lunch and Learn program where team members share knowledge with each other, and a Communities of Interest program that connects people around shared disciplines and curiosities. Growth is part of the job here, not a reward for surviving it. Does HatchWorks have an internship program? Yes. The internship program runs twice a year and gives participants real project work, not busy work. Keep an eye on the jobs board for current openings. Is there room to move up within the company? Yes. HatchWorks has grown consistently and that creates real paths upward. We track performance, recognize initiative, and promote from within when people are ready. Your trajectory here is largely up to you. Is HatchWorks fully remote? We are remote friendly. You can work from home or from one of our HatchHubs. Most roles give you the flexibility to choose where you work best, while staying connected with the broader team. Are part-time or flexible arrangements possible? We consider flexible arrangements case by case. If that matters to you, bring it up early in the process. We would rather know upfront than have it become an issue later. Still have a question not covered here? Reach out at connect@hatchworksai.com or contact the recruiter listed on the specific position you are interested in. We are happy to answer directly. title: Careers at Honeybadger
text: Careers at Honeybadger We're a small, private company with no outside funding, and we don't subscribe to the hustle ethic that is common to much of the technology industry. We don't currently have any openings. If you want to be among the first to know about new openings at Honeybadger, you can sign up for our job announcement list: Keep me posted How we work Working at Honeybadger isn't crazy. We work to live, rather than live to work. We're a small, private company with no outside funding, and we don't subscribe to the hustle ethic that is common to much of the technology industry. Instead, we put ourselves, our families, and our health first by working at a sustainable pace (30-hour work-weeks) to provide an excellent service to awesome customers. We work remotely and independently We don't have an office, and we like it that way. You can work from home, from a coworking space, or from a coffee shop — the choice is yours to work how you like. We also don't do Agile, Scrum, or any other methodology that has name, and we don't pair regularly. Our "process" is pretty light... we decide what we want to build, often based on what our customers have requested, and then we go build it. We aim to ship regularly — we get antsy when we haven't shipped something to production in the past few days. We communicate asynchronously We do like to hang out in Slack and shoot the breeze from time to time, but real work happens in GitHub, so you can synchronize on your schedule. And it's no problem if you want to turn off Slack so you can get some deep work done. We all like to be heads-down on our tasks from time to time. We hire people who can manage themselves We aren't interested in micro-managing employees. Before founding Honeybadger, we were used to working independently as freelancers, and we continue to value being able to choose what we work on and how. As a result, we hire people who can do the same. We automate everything Everything that can be automated will be automated. There's no reason for us to have to push a button or type some commands to scale our servers when we can set up an AWS autoscaling group to do that for us. And instead of shipping shirts out ourselves, we're happy to pay Printfection to do that for us. Whenever it makes sense to automate something, we do, so that we can move on to more interesting ways to spend our time. Naturally, we have a CI/CD process (using GitHub Actions) that deploys code to production without any humans involved, once a PR has been approved. We document everything Like our belief in automation, our belief in documentation saves our time as well as our sanity. If we have a process to follow, we document it, so we can (hopefully) automate it, or at least make it as brainless as possible. If a question pops up time and again in customer support, we document the answer so we don't have to keep rediscovering the answer ourselves. :) We love to learn We feel that life without learning is just too boring. We aim to always be learning new techniques and new technologies to keep things fresh. We take care of ourselves Finally, this business exists to take care of our customers and ourselves. We pay 100% of health insurance premiums for U.S. employees and their dependents, we match 401k contributions up to 4% of salary, and we provide a generous vacation and holiday policy. Simplify your life with Honeybadger Get monitoring done. Get real-time alerts when code breaks, monitor performance, and fix errors in record time. Start free trial Book a demo

text: Careers at IdeawareRemote software developer jobs for Latin American engineers, working full time with US startups in fintech, healthtech and AI. See open roles and apply.Want to work on products people actually use? At Ideaware, you collaborate directly with U.S. startups building fintech platforms, healthcare technology, and AI-powered SaaS. You’re part of the product team. You work alongside senior engineers, ship features that matter, and build your career with companies solving real problems.We’re hiring talented engineers, designers, and product people who want to work on challenging projects without relocating. You get the quality of U.S. startup work (modern stack, real ownership, career growth) without the typical remote work problems (timezone chaos, micromanagement, being treated like a second-class citizen). If you want to work on products that actually ship, check the openings above or apply here.What You’ll Actually GetWork with real startups. You’ll collaborate directly with U.S. companies building products that matter. Not agencies, not outsourcing shops, actual product teams.Remote flexibility. Work from home, work from the office, work from a coffee shop. As long as you’re delivering and available during core hours, we don’t care where you are.Real projects. You’ll work on products used by thousands of people. Fintech platforms, analytics SaaS, healthcare technology, AI-powered tools. Not boring enterprise dashboards or maintenance work no one else wants to do.Career growth. We promote from within. Engineers become tech leads. Tech leads become engineering managers. Designers become design leads. If you’re good and you want to grow, we’ll help you get there.Get paid in USD. Competitive salaries paid in U.S. dollars, not “competitive for the region.” Your compensation reflects the value you create and the quality of work you deliver.Modern stack. React, Node.js, Ruby on Rails, Python, AWS, AI/ML tools. We use the technologies that make sense for the project, not whatever legacy system the client is stuck with.No BS culture. We don’t do performative work. No daily status reports, no fake urgency, no pointless meetings. You get clear expectations, autonomy to do your job, and support when you need it.If you’re the kind of engineer or designer who wants to work on products that actually matter and be treated like a professional instead of a contractor, we should talk. title: Full-Stack Engineer (Mid–Senior, TypeScript)
text: RemoteFull-Stack Engineer (Mid–Senior, TypeScript)Remote · Full-timeHotFull-timeIn the next weekRemoteFull-time$4,000 – $4,500Hiring: In the next weekAbout the roleWe're building a multi-tenant, white-label telehealth platform — think "Shopify for telemedicine": clinics get branded storefronts, doctor and patient portals, e-prescribing, payments, and pharmacyfulfillment, all switchable per tenant. The architecture (plugin-based modular monolith, tenant isolation, CI gates) is established; you'll build product features on top of it, end to end — schemato API to UI — with clear specs and an experienced engineer to review your work.Small team, high velocity, story-driven backlog. You'll ship to staging in your first week.What you'll doBuild features across the stack: Prisma models → NestJS services/controllers → React portal pagesImplement stories from written acceptance criteria within our plugin architecture (catalog, ordering, messaging, patient/doctor portals, fulfillment)Integrate third-party APIs following established patterns: webhooks, payment providers, shipping/trackingWrite background job handlers (BullMQ queues, retries, idempotency) for order and prescription flowsFollow — and learn to reason about — our safety invariants: tenant isolation via Postgres RLS, entitlement gating, audit loggingWrite unit tests with every feature; keep CI green (typecheck, lint, tests are merge gates)Participate in code review, both giving and receivingTech stackLanguage: TypeScript everywhere, strict modeBackend: Node.js, NestJS, Prisma ORMDatabase: PostgreSQL 16 (multi-schema, row-level security), Redis + BullMQFrontend: React + Vite, TanStack Query + Router, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, react-hook-form + zodMonorepo: Nx + pnpm workspaces with enforced module boundariesTesting: Vitest (unit), Playwright (e2e)CI/CD: GitHub Actions, staging-first flow, health-gated deploys (no Docker/Kubernetes)Nice to have (we'll teach you the rest)Multi-tenant SaaS exposure: feature flags, per-tenant config, tenant data isolationRow-level security, or any serious thinking about data isolationHealthcare or another regulated domain (audit trails, PII/PHI handling)E-commerce flows: carts, checkout, payments, fulfillmentMessage queues / background jobs in productionAI-assisted development workflows (we lean into them heavily)How we workThe task ID is the primary key: every branch, commit, and PR traces to a tracked work itemQuality gates on every merge: typecheck, lint, unit tests — non-negotiableSafety rules are enforced in code, not convention: no prescription, no shipment; disabling a module never deletes data; no tenant context means zero rowsDaily written reports over meetings; Slack is an inbox, never the system of recordWhat you'll getReal end-to-end ownership of features, not tickets in a siloA codebase with working examples of every pattern you'll need — and review that explains the why, not just the whatGrowth path toward senior: architecture involvement, integration design, and increasing autonomy as you demonstrate itRequirements3–5 years building production web applications, with solid TypeScript on both backend and frontendHands-on experience with a typed backend framework (NestJS a plus — or Express/Fastify with discipline, or similar DI-based frameworks)Comfortable with relational databases: schema design, migrations, writing and debugging real queriesHave consumed or built REST APIs with proper validation and error handling; understand webhooks and idempotency at least conceptuallyTest-writing is part of your definition of done, not a choreCan take a well-written story with acceptance criteria and deliver it with minimal hand-holding — and know when to ask instead of guessingClear written communication; Department: OperationsLocation: ChileDescriptionEn Imagemaker estamos buscando nuestro próximo Desarrollador Fullstack Java/React. El cargo existe para apoyar la migración tecnológica completa de un portal de ventas heredado. Esta iniciativa forma parte de la adopción del nuevo stack tecnológico y de los lineamientos de arquitectura impulsados actualmente por cliente.El problema concreto que deberá resolver la persona es comprender las lógicas de negocio existentes en una aplicación desarrollada en .NET 6 con Angular y trasladarlas a una nueva solución basada en Java, Quarkus, MuleSoft y Hasura para el backend y las integraciones, y React para el frontend. La migración comprenderá el 100% de la aplicación y se ejecutará gradualmente, migrando, probando y validando los servicios de manera sucesiva.Se espera una persona full stack con mayor fortaleza en backend, pero que también cuente con conocimientos de React para trabajar en el frontend y consumir los servicios desarrollados durante la migración. Debe ser capaz de leer y comprender el código existente en .NET, trabajar con autonomía en las tareas de programación e implementar la arquitectura y los patrones ya definidos por el equipo. No deberá mantener la solución actual ni diseñar una nueva arquitectura.Key ResponsibilitiesResponsabilidades operativasMigrar: serás responsable de trasladar la totalidad de las lógicas de negocio desde .NET 6 al nuevo stack tecnológico.Implementar: serás responsable de desarrollar los servicios backend con Java y Quarkus bajo la arquitectura hexagonal definida.Integrar: serás responsable de conectar Quarkus, MuleSoft y Hasura mediante GraphQL y API REST.Desarrollar: serás responsable de adaptar el frontend en React para consumir correctamente los servicios migrados.Garantizar: serás responsable de entregar cada servicio migrado, probado y funcionando antes de avanzar al siguiente componente.Conectar: serás responsable de integrar la solución con las funciones AWS Lambda existentes y AWS Secrets Manager.Responsabilidad de coordinación técnicaCoordinar: serás responsable de gestionar los cambios mediante Git, evitando conflictos con el equipo que mantiene activa la aplicación actual.Skills, Knowledge and ExpertiseImprescindibles — Must-haveJava y Quarkus: experiencia sólida desarrollando servicios backend con Java y Quarkus.MuleSoft y Hasura: experiencia trabajando con ambas tecnologías dentro de una capa de integración.React: experiencia desarrollando frontend y consumiendo los servicios creados durante la migración.Desarrollo backend: aproximadamente cinco años de experiencia en desarrollo de software..NET 6: capacidad para leer y comprender código, estructuras por capas, tipos de objetos e inyección de dependencias; no se requiere dominio avanzado.GraphQL: experiencia implementando integraciones y exponiendo o consumiendo servicios mediante GraphQL.Microservicios y API REST: experiencia desarrollando microservicios y su comunicación mediante API REST.Arquitectura hexagonal: conocimiento suficiente para implementar una arquitectura previamente definida bajo este enfoque.AWS Lambda: experiencia integrando servicios con funciones Lambda existentes; no se requiere crearlas ni mantenerlas.AWS Secrets Manager: experiencia implementando conexiones con este servicio.Git: experiencia trabajando con repositorios, ramas y equipos que realizan modificaciones simultáneas sobre una misma solución.Autonomía técnica: capacidad para navegar por código heredado y resolver de manera autónoma dudas de programación, estructura, objetos e inyección de dependencias.Deseables — Nice-to-haveMigraciones tecnológicas: experiencia previa migrando aplicaciones desde .NET hacia Java o Quarkus.Spring Boot: experiencia senior en Java con Spring Boot cuando no se cuente con experiencia directa en Quarkus.GitHub Copilot: experiencia utilizando la herramienta para apoyar tareas de desarrollo.Coordinación técnica: para el perfil senior, capacidad para organizar el trabajo del equipo y apoyar la resolución de dudas técnicas.BeneficiosTenemos muy buenos beneficios para ti!🏖️ Don’t worry, be happy: 3 días libres al año adicionales a tus vacaciones.✨ Permiso sin goce de sueldo para cumplir tus sueños.⚖️ Programa de bienestar enfocado a equilibrar el trabajo y la vida personal.🏥 Seguro Complementario 100% gratuito para Makers.🤓 ¡Programas de formación, clases de inglés y mucho más!🎂 Día libre para tu cumpleaños y medio día para los cumpleaños de tus hijos.💰 Bonificaciones que dan respiros: Fiestas patrias, navidad, matrimonio/AUC, nacimiento/adopción de hijos, etc.💳 Convenios y precios preferenciales con bancos.👶🏻 3 Días adicionales para padres por nacimiento o adopción de hijo/a.🐶 Convenio de seguro para tus mascotas!🌿 Nuestra cultura es horizontal, de innovación, desafiante y sobre todo, se respira mucha buena onda!En el marco de nuestro compromiso con la inclusión, la siguiente vacante está abierta en el marco de la ley 21.015. text: We are a worker-owned, employee-run company with more than 20 years of experience building open source software in a wide range of exciting fields. See our open positions and join us! “A great place to work” is an understatement! We care about one another, and our industry as a whole. Remote-friendly Collaborative and supportive environment Democratic, consensus-based assembly structure We provide a remote-friendly, collaborative, and supportive environment in which Igalians from around the globe participate equally in the management and decision-making process of the company via our democratic, consensus-based assembly structure. We feel a deep and continual obligation to acknowledge and counter the structural discrimination that permeates our industry and world. We believe that one of the best ways to do this is to grow and maintain the diversity of Igalia itself. In a practical sense, this also means that we use principles of diversity and inclusion to help shape company policy and to maintain a safe and just work environment. At Igalia you can develop your career in a unique environment, contributing to a vast array of projects such as work on widely-deployed projects like the WebKit, Blink and Gecko browser engines, Mesa graphics drivers, V8, JavaScriptCore and SpiderMonkey language runtimes, GStreamer multimedia toolkit or the Linux kernel. title: Careers at Human Made
text: Home » Careers Careers at Human Made A remote team building the future of the web Human Made is a fully remote, globally distributed agency with a people-first culture. We put humans at the heart of everything we do, valuing inclusivity, flexibility, autonomy, and transparency in how we work and grow together. What it’s like to be a Human Made human Our culture is built around people: our clients, colleagues, and collaborators. Whether you’re freelance or full-time, we work with respect, empathy, and a shared commitment to doing great work together. We support each other to grow, share knowledge freely, and approach every challenge with a mindset of continuous learning. It’s how we stay curious, sharp, and kind. Our open Employee Handbook Everyone is Human We are an equal opportunities employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability status. We are committed to creating a diverse environment that every team member feels proud to be part of, and welcome applications from any people in any country across the world. Being yourself at work Having zero tolerance for discrimination and bias is a given, but true inclusion goes further. Everyone should feel safe and supported in being themselves at work; after all, it’s what makes you ‘you’. We stand proudly alongside our colleagues, friends, clients, and partners in the LGBTQIA+ community to celebrate the diversity, richness, and differences that make us ‘us’. We’re hiring humansjust like you We’re always on the lookout for curious, capable, and compassionate people to join our team. Whether you’re a seasoned engineer, a strategist at heart, or someone who simply loves solving complex problems with open source, we’d love to hear from you. Don’t see a role that fits right now? We’re open to speculative applications. Reach out to hiring@humanmade.com. title: Building your software. Anywhere it needs to be.
text: Building your software. Anywhere it needs to be. Infinite Red is known world-wide as the U.S.-based software agencywhen you want the highest quality software and top-notch team. Our highly skilled software developers (averaging 15 years of professional software development experience) have built hundreds of apps across mobile, web, desktop, and beyond in technologies such as React Native, Expo, Swift, and Kotlin over the last decade, and now are leading the way in agentic coding. Let's talk about your project → Infinite Red's reputation comes from more than a decade in software development. Infinite Red's team of highly experienced U.S.-based engineers has been building impactful software for over a decade. We've been around long enough to know how this industry works and what makes great software. You may have heard about us from our work in React Native; that's because we host hundreds of developers in Portland at our Chain React conference, produce the popular React Native Radio podcast, and create and contribute to open source like Ignite and more. Bring us the software challenge in front of you. We'll help your team understand the tradeoffs, make sound decisions together, and move the work forward. Working with Infinite Red will be the least stressful part of your project. Let's see how we can help you → Your guide to all things React Native When it comes to React Native, we are second to none. Our software engineers have worked with React Native to build mobile, web, and desktop apps for nearly a decade. We maintain some of the most popular React Native open source software.We also host the USA’s only React Native conference, publish the React Native Newsletter, and produce the React Native Radio Podcast. title: 10 Essential React Native Developer Skills for Job Success
text:
Builder briefFormatguideStackReact NativeReading time15 minThis tutorial aims to provide software developers with a comprehensive guide on the essential skills required for success as a React Native developer. We will cover various topics ranging from JavaScript fundamentals to UI design and layout, state management, testing, and debugging. By mastering these skills, you will be well-equipped to tackle real-world React Native development projects and increase your chances of securing a job in this field. Section 1: JavaScript Fundamentals​ Understanding ES6+ features​ ES6 introduced several important features that have become widely adopted in modern JavaScript development. It is crucial for React Native developers to have a solid understanding of these features. Let's explore some of them in detail: Working with arrow functions​ Arrow functions provide a concise syntax for creating functions in JavaScript. They offer some advantages over traditional function declarations, such as lexical scoping of this and implicit return of single expressions. Here's an example: const sum = (a, b) => a + b;console.log(sum(2, 3)); // Output: 5 In the above code, we define an arrow function called sum that takes two parameters a and b and returns their sum. The function is then invoked with the arguments 2 and 3, resulting in the output 5. Using destructuring assignment​ Destructuring assignment allows us to extract values from arrays or objects and assign them to variables in a concise manner. It can greatly simplify working with complex data structures. Here's an example: const person = { name: 'John', age: 25 };const { name, age } = person;console.log(name); // Output: Johnconsole.log(age); // Output: 25 In the above code, we define an object person with properties name and age. We then use destructuring assignment to extract the values of these properties into variables with the same names. Finally, we log the values of name and age, resulting in the output John and 25, respectively. Understanding closures​ Closures are an important concept in JavaScript that enables data encapsulation and private variables. They are created when a function is defined within another function and has access to the outer function's variables. Here's an example: function outerFunction() { const message = 'Hello'; function innerFunction() { console.log(message); } return innerFunction;}const func = outerFunction();func(); // Output: Hello In the above code, we define an outer function outerFunction that declares a variable message and defines an inner function innerFunction that logs the value of message. The outer function returns the inner function, which is then assigned to the variable func. When func is invoked, it accesses the message variable from its outer scope and logs its value, resulting in the output Hello. Section 2: React Basics​ Understanding React components​ React components are the building blocks of any React application. They encapsulate reusable UI elements and their behavior. It is essential to understand the different types of components and how to create and use them effectively. Let's explore this topic further: Working with JSX​ JSX is a syntax extension for JavaScript that allows you to write HTML-like code within your JavaScript files. It is a fundamental part of React development and enables the declarative rendering of components. Here's an example: import React from 'react';function App() { return

Hello, React!

;}export default App; In the above code, we import the React module and define a functional component called App. Within the component's body, we use JSX to render an h1 element with the text "Hello, React!". Finally, we export the App component for use in other parts of our application. Using state and props​ State and props are two important concepts in React for managing component data and passing data between components. Understanding how to use them correctly is crucial for building dynamic and interactive applications. Here's an example: import React, { useState } from 'react';function Counter() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); const increment = () => { setCount(count + 1); }; return (

Count: {count}

);}export default Counter; In the above code, we import the useState hook from the react module to manage the component's state. We declare a state variable count and a function setCount to update its value. We define an increment function that increments the count value when the button is clicked. Finally, we render the current count value and a button that triggers the increment function. Handling events​ React provides a convenient way to handle user events and perform actions in response to them. It is important to understand how to attach event handlers to elements and handle events correctly. Here's an example: import React from 'react';function Button() { const handleClick = () => { alert('Button clicked!'); }; return ;}export default Button; In the above code, we define a functional component Button that renders a button element. We declare a handleClick function that displays an alert when the button is clicked. We attach the handleClick function to the button's onClick event using JSX syntax. Section 3: React Native Fundamentals​ Setting up a React Native project​ Setting up a React Native project involves installing the necessary dependencies and configuring the development environment. It is important to be familiar with this process to start building React Native applications. Let's explore the steps involved: Navigating between screens​ Navigation is a crucial aspect of mobile app development. React Native provides various navigation solutions that allow users to move between different screens within an app. Let's explore one popular navigation library, React Navigation: import React from 'react';import { NavigationContainer } from '@react-navigation/native';import { createStackNavigator } from '@react-navigation/stack';import HomeScreen from './screens/HomeScreen';import DetailScreen from './screens/DetailScreen';const Stack = createStackNavigator();function App() { return ( );}export default App; In the above code, we import the necessary modules from the @react-navigation/native and @react-navigation/stack packages. We define a Stack component using the createStackNavigator function and configure it with the desired screens. Finally, we wrap our app components with the NavigationContainer component to enable navigation functionality. Working with components and styling​ React Native provides a set of built-in components that allow you to build user interfaces for mobile apps. It is essential to understand how to use these components effectively and apply styles to create visually appealing interfaces. Here's an example: import React from 'react';import { View, Text, StyleSheet } from 'react-native';function App() { return ( Hello, React Native! );}const styles = StyleSheet.create({ container: { flex: 1, justifyContent: 'center', alignItems: 'center', }, text: { fontSize: 24, fontWeight: 'bold', },});export default App; In the above code, we import the necessary modules from the react-native package. We define a functional component App that renders a View component as the root container and a Text component as the child element. We apply styles to the container and text using the StyleSheet API. Using APIs and libraries​ React Native provides access to various APIs and libraries that enable you to interact with device features and integrate third-party functionality into your app. It is important to be familiar with using these APIs and libraries effectively. Here's an example: import React from 'react';import { View, Text, Button, Linking } from 'react-native';function App() { const openURL = () => { Linking.openURL('https://www.example.com'); }; return ( Welcome to my app!

Oct 14 2026 • Alex Yumashev Setting up a helpdesk team Here's a situation we hear about from customers all the time. Someone gets hired as an IT support manager. They inherit two techs, a shared inbox (or a ticketing system nobody likes), and a mandate that sounds something like "build us a proper tiered support team." They have six months to show it's working. It's tempting to start shopping for software. But first you need to find out why everyone hates the current setup. A new ticketing system won't help much if the real problem is that nobody knows who's supposed to approve a laptop. Sep 27 2026 • Alex Yumashev Do people actually use AI support? We've analysed dozens of Reddit threads on r/sysadmin and here's what we've found: the people who run help desks for a living are not impressed. They aren't all hostile, though. Somewhere between "nobody wants this" and a vendor promising 90% deflection, a handful of admins have quietly got AI doing useful work. It just isn't the work the demos show. Sep 25 2026 • Alex Yumashev Best AI helpdesk solutions in 2026 Every helpdesk vendor now sells "AI". What they actually ship differs a lot. Some offer a chatbot that answers customers before a ticket exists. Some offer a copilot that drafts replies for agents. Others hand you a platform and a consultant's invoice. The pricing models differ too: per seat, per conversation, per "resolution", or a pool of credits that nobody on the buying committee fully understands.

title: Your coding agent can now work with massive video and sensor data
text: Trusted by startups and Fortune 500 companiesOur pedestrian detector regressed in night rain. Find the failures, figure out what they have in common, and build a dataset we can evaluate the fix against.One agent. Data flows from Collection (the fleet) through three stages handled by DataChain: Ingestion, compute what nobody labelled; Curation, assemble and version the set; and Loading, stream it into the training set. One store, many questions. Collection and Training (your model) are outside DataChain.One question. Four different kinds of workFinding the failures reads existing recordings to locate model errors.Finding common patterns extracts new signals shared by the failures.Building the eval set saves selected examples as a new dataset.Evaluating the fix hands the dataset to training to test improvements.Failure investigationFrom a regression to the exact recordings and failure cases behind it, then uncover the shared signals that explain what went wrong.Dataset curationFrom scattered files, recordings, labels, and metadata to a reproducible, versioned dataset ready for evaluation or model training.Large-scale processingFrom a local Python prototype to the same workload running efficiently across millions of files and hundreds of machines.Follow-up researchFrom an expensive first analysis to new questions that reuse existing results, code, datasets, and state instead of starting from scratch.Failure investigationFrom a regression to the exact recordings and failure cases behind it, then uncover the shared signals that explain what went wrong.Dataset curationFrom scattered files, recordings, labels, and metadata to a reproducible, versioned dataset ready for evaluation or model training.Large-scale processingFrom a local Python prototype to the same workload running efficiently across millions of files and hundreds of machines.Follow-up researchFrom an expensive first analysis to new questions that reuse existing results, code, datasets, and state instead of starting from scratch.What our customers sayDataChain added real value to our workflows - versioned datasets, automated ETL, and MLOps, all in Python. Something went wrong while submitting the form.Your Weekly SaaS PlaybookTo: YouFrom: ScaleworksThe future of vertical software; Manage time like an Amazon executive; Where to find your early adopters… The Beauty of Vertical SaaS🔧 For a while, many venture investors avoided vertical software because they felt its comparatively small markets would not produce target VC outcomes. That has of course changed in recent years, and CRV does a nice job of outlining why. They use the example of auto repair software – with 167k auto repair shops in the US and the lower priced players charging $2.7k a year, you conservatively have a ~$440M TAM (not the $1B+ venture gets excited about). But over time these software are able to further specialize and innovate within their verticals, both creating more solutions (more things to charge for) and improving their current offerings (giving them the ability to charge more), thus growing their TAM. What CRV is most excited about in vertical software is embedded commerce. Using the same example, embedded commerce would be selling auto parts directly through auto repair software, putting your website, booking system, POS, etc. all in one place.Scaling great productsinto great businessesCopyright © 2021. title: Senior AI Compute Infrastructure Engineer @ Kraken
Do work that reaches real users.
text: CareersDo work that reaches real users.We build production software for real users, in small Pods, since 2007. What you ship matters here. Where you sit does not.See open positions Browse the job board4.5 on Glassdoor, across 89 reviewsRemote first, hired across time zonesProduct work for real users, not tickets in a queueMeet usWe are a distributed team of designers, engineers, QA specialists, delivery managers, and operators, building digital products since 2007 from Barranquilla and wherever our people live. Respect and discipline shape how we work.“Our team is our greatest asset, and we pride ourselves on creating a culture where employees feel challenged, valued, and inspired. Over time, Koombea has established a reputation for being a great place to work, and we are extremely proud of that.Jonathan Tarud Koombea CEORemote firstWe hire where the talent is, not where a building is. Pods are put together across time zones, and the work is organized around that rather than in spite of it.That shows up in how a day actually runs. Decisions land in writing so nobody has to be awake to be included, and you are measured on what you ship rather than on the hours a tracker recorded. Async by default, with decisions written down Enough overlap with your Pod to pair, review, and unblock Judged on the work, not on time at a desk Set your own hours around the people you build withKoombea's teamEvery Pod is cross-disciplinary, so whichever of these is your craft, you work next to the other seven every day. We hire people who care about the product behind the ticket and write their decisions down. UI/UX Design Mobile Development Sales and Marketing Project Management Front-End Development Quality Assurance DevOps Back-End DevelopmentThe teamWe get together when it helps and work apart the rest of the time. Either way, the work happens in the open.Working a problem Small groups, one screen, decisions made in the room or in the thread.Pods, not departments Design, engineering, and QA on the same problem at the same time.Getting together Time in the same place is a choice, not a condition of the job.Employee benefitsOur people matter. These are the things that come with the job, wherever you happen to work from.Remote by defaultWork from anywhere that fits your needs. The team is spread across several countries and the job was written for that from the start.Flexible work hoursSet your schedule around the hours your Pod needs to overlap.Paid time offPaid holidays and paid time off you can use when you need to disconnect.Health insuranceMedical, dental, vision, and life insurance options for you and your family.Wellness and growthSupport for mental health, professional development, and role-specific learning.Competitive paySalary measured against the market, plus a 401(k) match.What people say about working hereWe would rather you heard it from the team than from us. These are the Glassdoor numbers as they stand today, including the ones we are still working on. We do not curate them.4.5 Overall rating on GlassdoorAcross 89 reviewsDiversity and inclusion 4.7 Culture and values 4.6 Work/life balance 4.3 Compensation and benefits 4.3 Senior management 4.1 Career opportunities 3.9 Would recommend to a friend93%Approve of the CEO96%Positive business outlook72%Read the reviews on GlassdoorOpen positionsEvery role is remote. Applications go straight to our job board, and a person on our team reads them.See every openingEverything here is delivered by an AI Pod: a committed scope, priced in story points, shipped in two-week cycles.How AI Pods workBring us the backlog.In 30 minutes, we will show you what a Pod would ship first and how we would price it.Book a Priority Sync

text: Slide 1 of 1Protect yourself from recruitment scams•Learn moreKentik CareersMake life awesome for people building and running the connected worldJoin our teamBring your full self, quirks and all. Join Kentik.BenefitsExcellent health, dental, and vision coverage (we cover 100% of premiums within the U.S. for you and any eligible dependents)Employer-funded health reimbursement account and monthly wellness stipendEmployer-paid short-term and long-term disability plans along with paid parental, family and medical leaveWork from whereyou are401(k) retirement accountCharitable donation matchingOpen PTO, a quarterly wellness day, and all public holidays in your countryHome office reimbursement and monthly stipends for phone and internetWhy work at KentikSlide 1 of 10“I love working at Kentik! How often do you hear folks saying they love where they work these days? We have innovative technology, incredibly talented and amazing people, and the culture is next to none. I have been working remotely for years and this is the first remote experience where I do not feel like I am on an island of one. We are collaborative as well as personable. We connect to work and connect as humans. I feel like I am supported and motivated to do my best work and I couldn’t be more excited that I get to do it here at Kentik!”Danielle TristaoDirector, Customer Success“Kentik is a truly unique place to work. There’s no shortage of network experts, happy to impart knowledge and help at a moment’s notice, which genuinely makes running our content strategy a dream come true. Beyond the technical expertise, this is a group of welcoming and kind people who really care about each other. When transparency and empathy start at the very top of a company, it’s easy to see how it’s adopted across the organization. Plus, we’re building the best network observability platform on earth, so that’s pretty rad, too.”David HallinanSr Director, Content Marketing“One thing I love about working at Kentik is the people. With my job, I get to work with a variety of folks across the company and I’m continually amazed with both their breadth of knowledge and their willingness to share it. I ask a lot of questions (I have to for my job), and they’re more than patient with me, some going even deeper into the subjects if I’m curious about why something is the way it is. title: Join our team
text: Join our teamLeadfeeder is the go-to-market platform for Europe and we’re on a mission to give businesses the data and insights they need to win leads and grow revenue. And we’re hiring! See open rolesEndorsed byOpen rolesNo roles match your filters.RevenueRemoteManager of Scaled Customer SuccessApply NowR&DRemoteSenior Data Engineer, Platform DataApply NowGet to know usWe want to know about you, but we'd also love for you to get to know us too!Recruiting is a 2-way streetThe hiring process works both ways and we'll provide you with all the information you'll need to get started with us. Learn about your tasks, team, manager, and what it's like to work with us!Be your true selfThe best advice we can give you is to be yourself throughout this journey. You're the central figure so we welcome you bringing your authentic self.Remote first and always connectedA flexible and remote work environment helps bring together great talent and enables long-term success and work/life balance. Regardless of our physical location, we enjoy working together, respect different time zones and working models, and enhance our experience by regularly meeting face-to-face. Stretch to growWe operate in a fast-growing environment and in a world of constant change. This requires everyone actively finding ways to constantly learn, grow and adapt. There is great learning opportunity in trying, failing, and trying again. Progress is made through iterations. Move the needleOur passion for meaningful output is manifested in our success. We focus on things that matter and make a difference when we deliver the most impactful results. Delivering relevant results at scale is what will ultimately lead to our success.Cultivate different perspectivesDiverse perspectives lead to better results. To contribute fully, all voices must feel included and valued. This enables greater collaboration as we co-create solutions, positively impacting our company, our products, our employees and our ecosystem. We embrace different cultures, backgrounds and demographics intentionally.Openness earns trustCommunication and expectation-setting increase trust and alignment. Sharing information transparently and listening with empathy helps us better understand each other’s perspective. Honest and constructive feedback helps us grow; seeking it out leads to better outcomes.Screening callDuring this call, a member of the Talent Acquisition team will have a chat with a candidate to cover some questions about experience and organizational matters. We'll share more about the role and Leadfeeder's culture. Skills InterviewUsually conducted by the hiring manager or someone you would be working closely with. Managers will ask skills-related questions pertinent to the job and provide more insight into the team, detailing what day-to-day activities will be like.Take-home assignmentWe'll send a brief with the details of a challenge to complete and present back to us. Candidate will meet with a number of people he/she'll be working closest with and will take them through findings from the assignment.Culture interviewThis interview will have a focus on culture and will help to picture how candidate may fit in culturally. Usually conducted by a member of the leadership team or a members of the team you would be working closely with.Your questions, answeredWhat can I expect after I apply? Straight after you apply you will receive an email from us letting you know we’ve received your application. Typically, between the application point and up to one week, you will be contacted by a member of the Talent team with an update on your application. What is the typical hiring process? Our hiring process has three to five stages tailored for each role. It starts with a Screening Call to discuss your career and role details. We will dive into your skills and experience. Next is the Skills Interview, giving a closer look at the team dynamics. Technical roles involve a practical evaluation. Roles requiring problem-solving and creativity include an At-Home Assignment and Follow-up Discussion. This step assesses your work approach and gives insight into the role's tasks. For some positions, there's a Culture Interview, a session to explore how well you fit with Leadfeeder's values and team. It's a chance to engage with team members, for certain positions you will meet a member of C Level. Our hiring process aims to evaluate your fit for the role and give a clear view of our company culture, ensuring mutual understanding and alignment of expectations and values.How long does it take to hire at Leadfeeder? The timeline can vary depending on the specific role and level, but in general, our process usually spans from the initial discussion with your talent partner to the final decision, which typically takes about 3 to 4 weeks. (We're crossing our fingers for a positive outcome for you!) Throughout this period, your talent partner will keep you informed and provide updates to ensure you are aware of what to anticipate, including any potential changes in the timeline.Who will I interact with during the process? You'll have the opportunity to interact with several members of the Leadfeeder team throughout the process, which will provide you with valuable insights from different angles. The individuals you meet can vary depending on the specific role, but in most instances, you can expect to engage with your talent partner, the potential manager or team leader, and potentially some of your future teammates.What steps can I take to get ready for my interview, and do you have any advice or suggestions? Tip 1: Be yourself. At Leadfeeder, we value and celebrate individuality and diverse perspectives. We encourage you to showcase your true personality and be your authentic self during the interview process because you shine brightest when you're being yourself. Tip 2: Keep it simple. We understand that interviews can be intimidating, and we've all been in your shoes before. The good news is that every member of the Leadfeeder team has gone through the same experience. So, take a deep breath, prepare your questions and examples of your past work, and trust that we'll guide you through the rest. Tip 3: Be well-prepared. Before your interview, familiarize yourself with Leadfeeder by exploring our website, products, careers page, and social media profiles. Research your interviewers on LinkedIn to learn about their backgrounds. The interview is a two-way process; ask questions about our culture, team, role, remote work, and the Leadfeeder experience.Can I use AI in the interview process? Be yourself in our interviews – open dialogue is key from your application onward. While AI can help, it won't replace human conversations at Leadfeeder. We value diversity and use AI to aid some applicants. Be genuine, and feel free to use AI for creativity, but if you're applying for an engineering role, turn off AI tools like GitHub Copilot during the interview.Grow your career with Leadfeeder todaySee open rolesFree 14-day trialNo credit card needed Instantly see your leads

title: Build The Future With Locus Robotics
text: Home > Company > Careers Build The Future With Locus Robotics Join a global team building the platform for modern fulfillment. We’re growing fast across robotics, AI, product, operations, and customer success — with roles available all over the world. Current Job Openings Our TeamWorking at Locus Robotics We take pride in our strong global team spirit, collaborative atmosphere, and terrific leadership. When you’re part of the Locus team, you’re working with the coolest robots in the industry (we might be biased, but our customers say it’s true!). To succeed at Locus, there are three requirements. You must be willing to work hard, work well with others, and be ready to have fun. When we all work together as one team, the opportunities for career growth and your own personal development are limitless. Core ValuesCore Values That Lead Our Success We act decisively We solve problems proactively, break down barriers, and take calculated risks. We operate with trust and integrity We respect one another. We work as a team and assume good intent. We do the right thing. We deliver results We set and meet high standards. We are accountable. We finish what we start and win as a team. We are inclusive We listen thoughtfully, and value ideas, passions, and curiosity. We innovate We think big and dig deep for solutions. CultureLife at Locus We all know the old adage of “work hard, play hard.” But at Locus, it is instead “work hard and have fun.” We make a point of hiring good people, and we all enjoy each other’s company daily and through Lunch and Learns, fun events, and our annual outings. Global Employer Celebrating Diversity Flexible Work Benefits Internships / Co-Op Locus University Global Employer Global Employer US, EMEA, APAC As our business has grown and expanded globally, our office locations have as well. Our global headquarters is in Wilmington, MA and our European headquarters is in Amsterdam. We are a truly global employer with positions available all over the world. Celebrating Diversity Celebrating Diversity Bring your whole self to work At Locus Robotics, we celebrate pride year-round, with comprehensive programs to welcome and support members of the LGBTQ+ community. From partner benefits, including healthcare, dental and life insurance, to all types of leave, we encourage everyone to bring their whole selves to work — no matter where you live, whom you love. Flexible Work Flexible Work Remote, hybrid, or on-site We have the right flexible work environment for everyone — remote, hybrid, or on-site — with the environment depending on the job responsibilities. At Locus, we understand that each individual and team works best differently, and we trust that you’ll put in your best work no matter where you’re working. Benefits Benefits Competitive, country-specific coverage Locus offers competitive benefits and personal time off that are specific to the country in which you work. Regardless of where you are, we have you covered with flexible programs that allow you to live life to the fullest. Programs include professional development, peer and company recognition programs, and a strong commitment to employee wellbeing and mental health. Internships / Co-Op Internships / Co-Op A strong start to your career At Locus, our internships and Co-Op program helps students learn about our real-world job environment, gain valuable experience in their chosen specialization, and develop skills that build a strong start to their career. You will gain valuable insights from leadership and your colleagues, create lasting relationships with your fellow interns, and work with our amazing global team! Locus University Locus University Keep learning and growing When you work at Locus Robotics, we want you to keep learning and growing through our robust internal learning and development programs. Locus University (our internal program) offers our employees no-cost, on-demand professional development to successfully onboard, enhance your career, and prepare for certifications. Build your skills in project management, leadership, communications, software, and more with over 135+ PDUs available for PMI certification.
